WalkthroughIntro.text: Welcome to FlowLedger. In the next few minutes, we will set up approvals, run an advance, and read the numbers.

Setup0-Organisation.text: First, your organisation. Add your branches, departments, cost codes and currencies. Every request in FlowLedger is filed against this structure.

Setup1-CreateRole.text: Next, roles. A role describes what someone does, like Disbursement Officer. Approval stages are assigned to roles, not to individual people.

Setup2-GrantPermissions.text: Now give the role its permissions. Tick exactly what it may do: approve requests, disburse funds, settle retirements. Everyone holding the role inherits them.

Setup3-InviteUser.text: Then invite your people. Here, Efua Owusu joins the Kumasi branch as a Disbursement Officer. Her approvals inbox follows from the roles she holds.

Setup4-CreateTemplate.text: With your people in place, create the workflow. One template per request type. Leave the branch blank, and it covers every branch.

Setup5-AddStages.text: Add the stages in order. First, approval by the requester's head of department, limited to their own department. Then finance approval. Then disbursement, where the funds are released.

Step1-CreateAdvance.text: Now the workflow is live. Ama Mensah needs funds for a field visit to Tamale. She raises an advance, adds each line item, and FlowLedger totals it in Ghana cedis.

Step2-SubmitRequest.text: One click submits it for approval. The request moves straight into the workflow. No emails, no chasing signatures.

Step3-ApproveRequest.text: Kwame, her head of department, finds it waiting in his approvals inbox. He reviews the details, adds a comment, and approves. It then moves on to finance and disbursement on its own.

Step4-DisburseAdvance.text: Once it is fully approved, Efua pays out the funds and records the payment voucher number. FlowLedger makes sure no one pays out a request they approved themselves.

Step5-RetireAdvance.text: After the trip, Ama retires the advance. She records what she actually spent, with receipts, and FlowLedger works out the difference. Here, one hundred and seventy cedis to refund.

Reports1-Cfo.text: For the CFO, the numbers are always current: spending month by month, advances that are still unaccounted for, and the cash available in every branch.

Reports2-It.text: And for IT and audit: approval times measured against your target, and a timestamped trail of every decision.

Outro.text: FlowLedger. Every advance approved, paid, and accounted for.

SetupOutro.text: Advances and expenses follow the same path: requester, head of department, finance, then disbursement. A retirement ends with a top-up, a refund, or a nil balance.

Promo1-Hook.text: Still chasing signatures for staff advances?

Promo4-Approve.text: Approvals follow your own workflow, and can be done in under a day.

Promo5-Disburse.text: Every payout lands in your cashbook.

Promo6-Retire.text: Retirements work out the refund for you.
